output.brief: Don't send the breach notice. The rise in lost bags is not a handler problem. Pelion uses the same Tessaly crew pool and its rate didn't move. Corvane bags that were read automatically stayed at the old rate. The whole increase sits in bags diverted to the manual encode desk. Those diversions rose from about 70 to about 460 a day, and 91% of the affected bags reached the lateral after it closed. The cause is the tag stock. Since 1 September, Corvane tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% on the old Brackwater stock. Brackwater tags used on counters on 14–16 Oct read normally, while kiosk tags printed on Fennick the same days still failed. Airport readers and other carriers' tags are unaffected. What we don't know yet is whether the stock is defective or just mismatched to the printer heat settings, and reduced kiosk cleaning may add to it. Next steps: switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater now (stock is held in stores until about December). Test Fennick with the printer manufacturer's guidance. Hold off on any claim against Fennick until the test result is in. Optionally, ask the airport to add a temporary encode workstation for the evening bank. I'm fairly confident in this.
